newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF plans 5,000 job cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF plans 5,000 job cuts - paper.

text.p: Defence electronics group Thomson CSF management has told union delegates that it expects to have to reduce its French workforce by 5,000 to about 32,000 by the end of 1997, Le Monde afternoon daily reported on Monday.
The company, contacted by Reuters, said it had no immediate comment to make.

Le Monde said Thomson-CSF had assessed the situation and decided on the basis of order-book expectations that it would have to reduce French staff levels by 5,000 from a level of 37,000 at the end of 1995, with a reduction 2,300 in 1996 and 2,700 in 1997.
This would follow a freeze on staff cuts imposed by former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur in 1993, the paper said.

Thomson-CSF is 58 percent-owned by Thomson SA, which is on the way to being privatised and taken over by Lagardere Groupe, with Lagardere planning to merge Thomson-CSF with its own Matra Defence Espace unit.

The newspaper also said Thomson-CSF management was counting on sales on the defence side to fall to 10 billion francs at the end of 1997 from 11.4 billion francs at the end of 1995 and for orders to slip to eight from 11 billion francs.
On the civil side, management was expecting an increase in sales to 29 billion francs by the end of 1997 from 24 billion francs at the end of 1995, the newspaper added.
